Elder & companion care.

Explore companionship and practical assistance that respect an older person’s routines, preferences and independence.

Companionship & everyday routines

Plan this care

Build support around a familiar routine.

Companionship starts with understanding the person’s day. Discuss where a helping hand would be welcome, what they enjoy and how support can respect their independence.

Before the conversation

  • The person’s interests and preferred daily routines
  • When company or practical assistance would be useful
  • Family involvement and the right level of support

Useful to discuss

  1. The everyday activities where help would be useful
  2. Mobility, supervision and companionship needs
  3. Personal routines, interests and preferences

Confirm the service scope, professional qualifications, timing and local availability before making arrangements.

Questions worth asking.

Take a short list into the conversation so the details are clear.

  • Which activities would benefit from a helping hand?
  • What routines and interests matter most?
  • Is assistance with mobility or supervision needed?
